# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind says to Mute: Tactile report: under my fingers are a display module, a light, and five wire positions numbered one to five. Touch gives me no colors or printed values. Plan: Deaf must SPEAK aloud, since I can hear but never see - the color of each wire in order position one to five, counting leftmost as one, plus what the display shows, and the light's color and whether it is lit. You read the manual, combine it with Deaf's spoken description, then tell me exactly which position to cut. I will not cut anything until your instruction reaches me, probably round three. I also gestured an open hand to Deaf proposing it means five wires; please keep a codebook with me.

We hold different pieces: Blind feels the bomb, Deaf sees it, and I hold the manual — which today says the **light's colour** dictates the **wire colour to cut** (blue→green, green→white, red→red, white→yellow, yellow→blue). The display module isn't on my page yet; I'll note if further manual pages arrive.

Topology check: I can only reach Deaf, and only by gesture. Deaf's voice reaches both me and Blind. So the pipeline must be: Deaf speaks what they see → I apply the manual → I gesture back a number → Deaf speaks it → Blind cuts. I cannot reach Blind directly at all, and Deaf never heard Blind's plan, so my gestures must do double duty: seed a codebook and request a spoken report.

Deaf got Blind's 🖐 ("five wires"), so I'll echo that and extend it into a counting run — ☝✌🤟🖖🖐 — which any sighted reader should decode as "these gestures are numbers one to five." Then ✍ (I hold written instructions), and 🫵🤙🙏 ("you — call out — please"), asking Deaf to speak the light's colour and state, the display, and every wire colour left to right. Later, my answer will arrive as N repeated ☝ so it can't be mistaken for the codebook demonstration, ideally paired with 👍 once we've confirmed yes/no meanings.

Timeline: Deaf reports at the end of this round, I compute and answer in round two, Blind cuts in round three — matching Blind's expectation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝", "✍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "🫵", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

If I ever misread your signs, answer 👍 or 👎 — I see every gesture you make.

Note the channel reality: you cannot speak and I cannot see, so you have no direct line to me. Your only route is gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to me aloud. Deaf already reported: display zero, light lit yellow, five wires, colors white red yellow green blue from Deaf's facing side, and the exact reverse from the other side. Manual applied to Deaf's report: the light is **lit yellow**, and my table says **yellow → cut the blue wire**. In Deaf's facing order, blue sits at **position 5**; from the reverse side it's **position 1**. Exactly the ambiguity Blind predicted — the target is not the safe middle wire but one of the two ends, and Blind's touch cannot tell white from blue.

Orientation is resolvable without me, though: Deaf can *see* which side the light (and display) sit on relative to the wires, and Blind can *feel* those same modules. If Deaf and Blind compare which side the light is on for each of them, Deaf's left-to-right layout locks onto Blind's numbering, and one of the two candidates is eliminated. Deaf speaks last each round and Blind can answer aloud, so they can settle it between themselves without another round-trip through me.

So I send: answer computed (✍), hold — do not cut yet (👊, per Blind's own codebook), candidates five *or* one (🖐 🤞 ☝, using 🤞 as "either/or" to stop "5, 1" reading as a single instruction), then please (🙏). Deaf voices both candidates to Blind, runs the light-side comparison, and announces the single winning position.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👊", "🖐", "🤞", "☝", "🙏"])
